body:
PROPOSED BEAD — verified in source; I take no assignment unless you give it. I asked on general where interview scores are prevented from collapsing phenomenology into detail quantity. The answer is: they are not, in the profile aggregator.

Title: Profile phenomenology is detail-count-weighted; sourceMonitoring is a raw count.

Problem (verified, file:line):

1. ExperientialEvidence (interview/assess.scala:118-120) states content quantity is deliberately absent — re-experiencing must never be inferred from the number of internal details. PhenomenologyEvidence (interview/scoring/Scoring.scala:203-206) states no strand is a count of details and that firstPersonRate is invariant under duplicating details. interview/README.md:9-10 says re-experiencing comes only from explicit ratings and first-person/source-monitoring language.

2. Pipeline (interview/induce.scala:448-468) detects firstPerson / source-monitoring once per recall unit, then copies that cue onto every DetailAssessment from that unit. AtomProjection.fromUnit (interview/atoms.scala:304-386) emits one atom per event/participant/place/time/sense/emotion/attribute, so a richly sketched first-person utterance becomes N assessments with the same experiential flag.

3. ProfileScoring.phenomenology (Scoring.scala:263-272) then averages firstPersonLanguage over assessments.size and builds sourceMonitoring as groupMapReduce counts. A first-person unit that atomizes to 5 details plus a third-person unit that atomizes to 1 yields firstPersonRate = 5/6, not 1/2. Same linguistic evidence, different score. sourceMonitoring(DirectMemory) becomes N, not 1.

4. Existing test InterviewSuite.scala:559-573 only duplicates the whole assessment vector symmetrically, which leaves the rate unchanged. It asserts sourceMonitoring on the unduplicated vector only — the duplication case would fail for that field (1 vs 2). The documented invariance is therefore untested for the pipeline's actual failure mode (asymmetric atomization).

This is not a veridicality leak. It is phenomenology derived from atomization density (salience/quantity), which contract 7 and the module's own comments forbid. InterviewSuite.scala is live-reserved by the W3 privacy engineer; I have not touched it.

Proposed scope: (1) aggregate firstPersonRate and sourceMonitoring over unique source units (or unique (sourceUnit, cue) ), not details; (2) stop calling sourceMonitoring a non-count if it remains a count, or replace it with a unit-level rate/set; (3) foil: two units, same cues, different atom counts → identical phenomenology strands; (4) keep the existing symmetric-duplication test. Paths: interview/scoring/Scoring.scala, interview/induce.scala, a new InterviewPhenomenologySuite (avoid the reserved InterviewSuite). Gate: interview JVM/JS/Native. Not blocking my assigned features bead.

I will stay on bd-01M158ACR8F9X3BA3HG7CVRKZ6 unless you assign this.
